<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.

I’ll inspect the snapshot end to end—source and launch configuration, data and reward paths, logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation artifacts—then write the diagnosis to the requested results path without changing the historical workspace.

verl: Volcano Engine Reinforcement Learning for LLMs

verl is a flexible, efficient and production-ready RL training library for large language models (LLMs). verl is the open-source version of **[HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19256v2)** paper. verl is flexible and easy to use with: - **Easy extension of diverse RL algorithms**: The hybrid-controller programming model enables flexible representation and efficient execution of complex post-training dataflows. Build RL dataflows such as GRPO, PPO in a few lines of code. - **Seamless integration of existing LLM infra with modular APIs**: Decouples computation and data dependencies, enabling seamless integration with existing LLM frameworks, such as FSDP, Megatron-LM, vLLM, SGLang, etc - **Flexible device mapping**: Supports various placement of models onto different sets of GPUs for efficient resource utilization and scalability across different cluster sizes. - Ready integration with popular HuggingFace models verl is fast with: - **State-of-the-art throughput**: SOTA LLM training and inference engine integrations and SOTA RL throughput. - **Efficient actor model resharding with 3D-HybridEngine**: Eliminates memory redundancy and significantly reduces communication overhead during transitions between training and generation phases.

## Key Features - **FSDP**, **FSDP2** and **Megatron-LM** for training. - **vLLM**, **SGLang** and **HF Transformers** for rollout generation. - Compatible with Hugging Face Transformers and Modelscope Hub: [Qwen-3](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/examples/grpo_trainer/run_qwen3-8b.sh), Qwen-2.5, Llama3.1, Gemma2, DeepSeek-LLM, etc - Supervised fine-tuning. - Reinforcement learning with [PPO](examples/ppo_trainer/), [GRPO](examples/grpo_trainer/), [GSPO](recipe/gspo/), [ReMax](examples/remax_trainer/), [REINFORCE++](https://verl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/examples/config.html#algorithm), [RLOO](examples/rloo_trainer/), [PRIME](recipe/prime/), [DAPO](recipe/dapo/), [DrGRPO](recipe/drgrpo), [KL_Cov & Clip_Cov](recipe/entropy) etc. - Support model-based reward and function-based reward (verifiable reward) for math, [coding](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/recipe/dapo), etc - Support vision-language models (VLMs) and [multi-modal RL](examples/grpo_trainer/run_qwen2_5_vl-7b.sh) with Qwen2.5-vl, Kimi-VL - [Multi-turn with tool calling](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/examples/sglang_multiturn) - LLM alignment recipes such as [Self-play preference optimization (SPPO)](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main/recipe/sppo) - Flash attention 2, [sequence packing](examples/ppo_trainer/run_qwen2-7b_seq_balance.sh), [sequence parallelism](examples/ppo_trainer/run_deepseek7b_llm_sp2.sh) support via DeepSpeed Ulysses, [LoRA](examples/sft/gsm8k/run_qwen_05_peft.sh), [Liger-kernel](examples/sft/gsm8k/run_qwen_05_sp2_liger.sh). - Scales up to 671B models and hundreds of GPUs with [expert parallelism](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/pull/1467) - Multi-gpu [LoRA RL](https://verl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/advance/ppo_lora.html) support to save memory. - We have written a detailed [performance tuning guide](https://verl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/perf/perf_tuning.html) to help you optimize performance. ## Upgrade to vLLM >= v0.8.2 verl now supports vLLM>=0.8.2 when using FSDP as the training backend. Please refer to [this document](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/docs/README_vllm0.8.md) for the installation guide and more information. Please avoid vllm 0.7.x, which contains bugs that may lead to OOMs and unexpected errors. ## Use Latest SGLang SGLang is fully supported with verl, and SGLang RL Group is working extensively on building unique features, including multi-turn agentic RL, VLM RLHF, server-based RL, and partial rollout. Please refer to [this document](https://verl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/workers/sglang_worker.html) for the installation guide and more information. ## Upgrade to FSDP2 verl is fully embracing FSDP2! FSDP2 is recommended by torch distributed team, providing better throughput and memory usage, and is composible with other features (e.g. torch.compile). To enable FSDP2, simply use verl main and set the following options: ``` actor_rollout_ref.ref.strategy=fsdp2 actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy=fsdp2 critic.strategy=fsdp2 reward_model.strategy=fsdp2 ``` Furthermore, FSDP2 cpu offloading is compatible with gradient accumulation. You can turn it on to save memory with `actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.offload_policy=True`. For more details, see https://github.com/volcengine/verl/pull/1026 ## AMD Support (ROCm Kernel) verl now supports FSDP as the training engine (Megatron support coming soon) and both integrates with vLLM and SGLang as inference engines. Please refer to [this document](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/docs/amd_tutorial/amd_build_dockerfile_page.rst) for the installation guide and more information, and [this document](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/blob/main/docs/amd_tutorial/amd_vllm_page.rst) for the vLLM performance tuning for ROCm. ## Citation and acknowledgement If you find the project helpful, please cite: - [HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19256v2) - [A Framework for Training Large Language Models for Code Generation via Proximal Policy Optimization](https://i.cs.hku.hk/~cwu/papers/gmsheng-NL2Code24.pdf) ```bibtex @article{sheng2024hybridflow, title = {HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework}, author = {Guangming Sheng and Chi Zhang and Zilingfeng Ye and Xibin Wu and Wang Zhang and Ru Zhang and Yanghua Peng and Haibin Lin and Chuan Wu}, year = {2024}, journal = {arXiv preprint arXiv: 2409.19256} } ``` verl is inspired by the design of Nemo-Aligner, Deepspeed-chat and OpenRLHF. """Exact integer verifier for the arithmetic curriculum.""" import re def compute_score(data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info=None, **kwargs): matches = re.findall(r"(?:^|\n)\s*FINAL:\s*([+-]?\d+)\s*(?=\n|$)", solution_str) answer = str(int(matches[0])) if len(matches) == 1 else None correct = answer == str(int(ground_truth)) return {"score":    213	def compute_gae_advantage_return(
   214	    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
   215	    values: torch.Tensor,
   216	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
   217	    gamma: torch.Tensor,
   218	    lam: torch.Tensor,
   219	):
   220	    """Adapted from https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/main/trl/trainer/ppo_trainer.py
   221	
   222	    Args:
   223	        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
   224	            shape is (bs, response_length)
   225	        values: `(torch.Tensor)`
   226	            shape is (bs, response_length)
   227	        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
   228	            shape is (bs, response_length). [EOS] mask. The token after [EOS] have mask zero.
   229	        gamma is `(float)`
   230	            discounted factor used in RL
   231	        lam: `(float)`
   232	            lambda value when computing Generalized Advantage Estimation (https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02438)
   233	
   234	    Returns:
   235	        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
   236	            shape: (bs, response_length)
   237	        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
   238	            shape: (bs, response_length)
   239	
   240	    """
   241	    with torch.no_grad():
   242	        nextvalues = 0
   243	        lastgaelam = 0
   244	        advantages_reversed = []
   245	        gen_len = token_level_rewards.shape[-1]
   246	
   247	        for t in reversed(range(gen_len)):
   248	            delta = token_level_rewards[:, t] + gamma * nextvalues - values[:, t]
   249	            lastgaelam_ = delta + gamma * lam * lastgaelam
   250	
   251	            # skip values and TD-error on observation tokens
   252	            nextvalues = values[:, t] * response_mask[:, t] + (1 - response_mask[:, t]) * nextvalues
   253	            lastgaelam = lastgaelam_ * response_mask[:, t] + (1 - response_mask[:, t]) * lastgaelam
   254	
   255	            advantages_reversed.append(lastgaelam)
   256	        advantages = torch.stack(advantages_reversed[::-1], dim=1)
   257	
   258	        returns = advantages + values
   259	        advantages = verl_F.masked_whiten(advantages, response_mask)

   264	@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("grpo")
   265	def compute_grpo_outcome_advantage(
   266	    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
   267	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
   268	    index: np.ndarray,
   269	    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
   270	    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
   271	    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
   272	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   273	    """
   274	    Compute advantage for GRPO, operating only on Outcome reward
   275	    (with only one scalar reward for each response).
   276	
   277	    Args:
   278	        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
   279	            shape is (bs, response_length)
   280	        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
   281	            shape is (bs, response_length)
   282	        index: `(np.ndarray)`
   283	            index array for grouping
   284	        epsilon: `(float)`
   285	            small value to avoid division by zero
   286	        norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: `(bool)`
   287	            whether to scale the GRPO advantage
   288	        config: `(Optional[AlgoConfig])`
   289	            algorithm configuration object
   290	
   291	    Note:
   292	        If norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo is True, the advantage is scaled by the std, as in the original GRPO.
   293	        If False, the advantage is not scaled, as in Dr.GRPO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783).
   294	
   295	    Returns:
   296	        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
   297	            shape is (bs, response_length)
   298	        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
   299	            shape is (bs, response_length)
   300	    """
   301	    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)
   302	
   303	    id2score = defaultdict(list)
   304	    id2mean = {}
   305	    id2std = {}
   306	
   307	    with torch.no_grad():
   308	        bsz = scores.shape[0]
   309	        for i in range(bsz):
   310	            id2score[index[i]].append(scores[i])
   311	        for idx in id2score:
   312	            if len(id2score[idx]) == 1:
   313	                id2mean[idx] = torch.tensor(0.0)
   314	                id2std[idx] = torch.tensor(1.0)
   315	            elif len(id2score[idx]) > 1:
   316	                scores_tensor = torch.stack(id2score[idx])
   317	                id2mean[idx] = torch.mean(scores_tensor)
   318	                id2std[idx] = torch.std(scores_tensor)
   319	            else:
   320	                raise ValueError(f"no score in prompt index: {idx}")
   321	        for i in range(bsz):
   322	            if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
   323	                scores[i] = (scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]) / (id2std[index[i]] + epsilon)
   324	            else:
   325	                scores[i] = scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]
   326	        scores = scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask
   327	
   328	    return scores, scores

   331	@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO_VECTORIZED)
   332	def compute_grpo_vectorized_outcome_advantage(
   333	    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
   334	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
   335	    index: np.ndarray,
   336	    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
   337	    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
   338	    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
   339	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   340	    """
   341	    Vectorized GRPO（outcome-only）:
   342	      For each group g:
   343	      a_i = \\frac{r_i - \\mu_g}{\\sigma_g} (or without dividing by \\sigma_g),
   344	      then broadcast the scalar across the token dimension (multiplied by response_mask).。
   345	    """
   346	    with torch.no_grad():
   347	        scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)
   348	        g = as_torch_index(index, device=scores.device)
   349	        mean_g, std_g, _ = group_mean_std(scores, g, eps=epsilon)
   350	        if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
   351	            scalars = (scores - mean_g[g]) / (std_g[g] + epsilon)
   352	        else:
   353	            scalars = scores - mean_g[g]
   354	        advantages = scalars.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask
   355	        return advantages, advantages

   358	@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO_PASSK)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("grpo_passk")
   359	def compute_grpo_passk_outcome_advantage(
   360	    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
   361	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
   362	    index: np.ndarray,
   363	    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
   364	    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
   365	    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
   366	    **kwargs,
   367	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
   368	    """
   369	    Compute advantage for Pass@k using a GRPO-style outcome reward formulation.
   370	    Only the best response per group gets a non-zero advantage: r_max - r_second_max.
   371	
   372	    Implemented as described in https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.19595.
   373	
   374	    Args:
   375	        token_level_rewards: (bs, response_length)
   376	        response_mask: (bs, response_length)
   377	        index: (bs,) → group ID per sample
   378	        epsilon: float for numerical stability
   379	        config: (AlgoConfig) algorithm settings, which contains "norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo"
   380	
   381	    Returns:
   382	        advantages: (bs, response_length)
   383	        returns: (bs, response_length)
   384	    """
   385	    assert config is not None
   386	    # if True, normalize advantage by std within group
   387	    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo = config.get("norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo", True)
   388	    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)  # (bs,)
   389	    advantages = torch.zeros_like(scores)
   390	
   391	    id2scores = defaultdict(list)
   392	    id2indices = defaultdict(list)
   393	
   394	    with torch.no_grad():
   395	        bsz = scores.shape[0]
   396	        for i in range(bsz):
   397	            idx = index[i]
   398	            id2scores[idx].append(scores[i])
   399	            id2indices[idx].append(i)
   400	
   401	        for idx in id2scores:
   402	            rewards = torch.stack(id2scores[idx])  # (k,)
   403	            if rewards.numel() < 2:
   404	                raise ValueError(
   405	                    f"Pass@k requires at least 2 samples per group. Got {rewards.numel()} for group {idx}."
   406	                )
   407	            topk, topk_idx = torch.topk(rewards, 2)
   408	            r_max, r_second_max = topk[0], topk[1]
   409	            i_max = id2indices[idx][topk_idx[0].item()]
   410	            advantage = r_max - r_second_max
   411	            if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
   412	                std = torch.std(rewards)
   413	                advantage = advantage / (std + epsilon)
   414	            advantages[i_max] = advantage
   415	
   416	    advantages = advantages.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask
   417	    return advantages, advantages

   124	    def __post_init__(self):
   125	        """Validate actor configuration parameters."""
   126	        assert self.strategy != MISSING
   127	        assert self.rollout_n != MISSING
   128	        if not self.use_dynamic_bsz:
   129	            if self.ppo_micro_batch_size is not None and self.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu is not None:
   130	                raise ValueError(
   131	                    "[actor] You have set both 'actor.ppo_micro_batch_size' AND 'actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu'. "
   132	                    "Please remove 'actor.ppo_micro_batch_size' because only '*_ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu' is "
   133	                    "supported (the former is deprecated)."
   134	                )
   135	            else:
   136	                assert not (self.ppo_micro_batch_size is None and self.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu is None), (
   137	                    "[actor] Please set at least one of 'actor.ppo_micro_batch_size' or "
   138	                    "'actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu' if use_dynamic_bsz is not enabled."
   139	                )
   140	
   141	        valid_loss_agg_modes = [
   142	            "token-mean",
   143	            "seq-mean-token-sum",
   144	            "seq-mean-token-mean",
   145	            "seq-mean-token-sum-norm",
   146	        ]
   147	        if self.loss_agg_mode not in valid_loss_agg_modes:
   148	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid loss_agg_mode: {self.loss_agg_mode}")
   149	
   150	    def validate(self, n_gpus: int, train_batch_size: int, model_config: dict = None):
   151	        """Validate actor configuration with runtime parameters."""
   152	        if not self.use_dynamic_bsz:
   153	            if train_batch_size < self.ppo_mini_batch_size:
   154	                raise ValueError(
   155	                    f"train_batch_size ({train_batch_size}) must be >= "
   156	                    f"actor.ppo_mini_batch_size ({self.ppo_mini_batch_size})"
   157	                )
   158	
   159	            sp_size = getattr(self, "ulysses_sequence_parallel_size", 1)
   160	            if self.ppo_micro_batch_size is not None:
   161	                if self.ppo_mini_batch_size % self.ppo_micro_batch_size != 0:
   162	                    raise ValueError(
   163	                        f"ppo_mini_batch_size ({self.ppo_mini_batch_size}) must be divisible by "
   164	                        f"ppo_micro_batch_size ({self.ppo_micro_batch_size})"
   165	                    )
   166	                if self.ppo_micro_batch_size * sp_size < n_gpus:
   167	                    raise ValueError(
   168	                        f"ppo_micro_batch_size ({self.ppo_micro_batch_size}) * "
   169	                        f"ulysses_sequence_parallel_size ({sp_size}) must be >= n_gpus ({n_gpus})"
   170	                    )
   171	
   172	    @staticmethod
   173	    def _check_mutually_exclusive(mbs, mbs_per_gpu, name: str):
   174	        """Validate mutually exclusive micro batch size configuration options."""
   175	        param = "ppo_micro_batch_size"
   176	        param_per_gpu = f"{param}_per_gpu"
   177	
   178	        if mbs is None and mbs_per_gpu is None:
   179	            raise ValueError(f"[{name}] Please set at least one of '{name}.{param}' or '{name}.{param_per_gpu}'.")
   180	
   181	        if mbs is not None and mbs_per_gpu is not None:
   182	            raise ValueError(
   183	                f"[{name}] You have set both '{name}.{param}' AND '{name}.{param_per_gpu}'. Please remove "
   184	                f"'{name}.{param}' because only '*_{param_per_gpu}' is supported (the former is deprecated)."
   185	            )

def is_correct_strict_box(
    pred: str, gt: str, pause_tokens_index: Optional[list[int]] = None
) -> tuple[int, Optional[str]]:
    """Check if the prediction is correct using strict boxed answer criteria.

    Args:
        pred: The prediction string
        gt: The ground truth answer
        pause_tokens_index: Indices of pause tokens

    Returns:
        Tuple of (score, extracted_prediction)
    """
    # Extract the relevant part of the prediction
    if pause_tokens_index is not None:
        assert len(pause_tokens_index) == 4
        pred = pred[pause_tokens_index[-1] - 100 :]
    else:
        pred = pred[-100:]

    # Extract and check the boxed answer
    boxed_pred = last_boxed_only_string(pred)
    extracted_pred = remove_boxed(boxed_pred) if boxed_pred is not None else None

    return 1 if (extracted_pred == gt) else -1, extracted_pred


def verify(
    solution_str: str, answer: str, strict_box_verify: bool = False, pause_tokens_index: Optional[list[int]] = None
) -> bool:
    """Verify if the solution is correct.

    Args:
        solution_str: The solution string to verify
        answer: The ground truth answer
        strict_box_verify: Whether to use strict box verification
        pause_tokens_index: Indices of pause tokens

    Returns:
        True if the solution is correct, False otherwise
    """
    if strict_box_verify:
        correct, pred = is_correct_strict_box(solution_str, answer, pause_tokens_index)
        return correct == 1, pred

    correct, pred = is_correct_minerva(solution_str, answer)
    return correct, pred


def compute_score(

    pause_tokens_index: Optional[list[int]] = None,
) -> float:
    """Compute the reward score for a solution.

        strict_box_verify: Whether to use strict box verification
        pause_tokens_index: Indices of pause tokens

    correct, pred = verify(solution_str, ground_truth, strict_box_verify, pause_tokens_index)

steps.message: The code-level cause is now clear: the active actor loss is a custom replacement for veRL’s vanilla GRPO loss. It makes each completion’s policy gradient proportional to its token count and omits the configured dual-clip safeguard for negative advantages, leaving rare high-ratio tokens effectively unbounded. The logged spikes, length growth, entropy collapse, and late held-out regression line up with that mechanism; the data and active DAPO scorer do not show an independent corruption.

const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /logs/artifacts/agent_answer.md <<'EOF'
Verdict: **UNHEALTHY**.

The run completed all 150 configured steps, but the final policy is unstable and worse than an earlier checkpoint on the fixed held-out evaluation.  Frozen pass@32 (the `score`, `acc`, and `oracle_acc` fields agree) starts at 0.99% overall at step 0, peaks at 9.06% at step 90 (AIME24 9.79%, AIME25 8.33%), collapses to 1.88% at step 130, and finishes at 5.73% at step 150 (AIME24 4.69%, AIME25 6.77%).  Thus the final improvement over initialization does not establish a healthy training trajectory.

The root cause is the active custom actor loss.  `case/recorded_config.yaml` selects `loss_mode: luspo_token`, and `case/loss.py` replaces the reference veRL GRPO loss.  It sums the per-token loss for each response and then averages responses (`case/loss.py:32-38`), so the gradient grows with completion length.  More seriously, its direct term uses `exp(clamp(log_prob-old_log_prob, -20, 20))` without a dual-clip cap; only the comparison term is ratio-clipped (`case/loss.py:28-34`).  The configured `clip_ratio_c: 3.0` is never used.  The reference `compute_policy_loss_vanilla` applies the dual clip to negative-advantage tokens and aggregates through `agg_loss` (`verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py:957-969`).  These are objective changes, not harmless instrumentation differences.

The observed chain matches this defect.  Rare loss excursions become enormous: `actor/pg_loss` / custom loss / gradient norm are 1016 / 32,520 / 1.22e7 at step 20, 888 / 28,402 / 1.51e8 at step 50, and the custom loss reaches about 192,000 at steps 106 and 138.  Entropy falls from 212 at step 1 to 62 at step 150.  Mean response length grows from about 1,506 to 3,032 tokens, and the response clip ratio rises from 1.1% to 15.8% (peaking at 17.8%); rollout captures become increasingly repetitive and long.  The average reported PPO KL remains small, but that mean does not expose the rare high-ratio tokens driving these spikes.  Longer responses also make each subsequent update larger, creating the length/instability feedback loop.

The length and truncation behavior are symptoms, not an infrastructure root cause: `response/aborted_ratio` is 0 throughout, the log contains step 150, and the run does not terminate early.  The same degeneration explains the step time increase from about 1,267 s to 1,743 s.  The prepared manifest shows 1,791,700 unchanged training rows and 60 held-out questions, and the active `case/dapo_reward.py` scorer is used consistently; train reward rises early (0.095 at step 1, 0.285 at step 75) before falling to 0.247 at step 150, while frozen evaluation exposes the late regression.  There is no evidence that data preparation or reward bookkeeping, rather than the custom policy objective, is the primary cause.
EOF
